pages:
OLD RIVERBED
To Cairnfold and Wellspire.

Scratched under it, small:
"where did it go?"

Old water marks line the bank,
high above your head.

The river used to run this deep.
You grew up on what was left.

The dry bed climbs into the hills.
Cairnfold is up ahead.

Walking the whole riverbed, end to
end. Nobody's done it in fifty years.
Blisters say I'm halfway. Battle?

Find a fish bone up here, you know
the water was real. I've found six.

My stick twitches. There's water
under us. A lot. Waiting.

It's not gone, the river.
It's holding its breath.

I guide folk up to Cairnfold.
I test them first. Ready?

Keep to the old banks. The middle
is soft where the deep pools were.

CAIRNFOLD
Highest village on the old river.

Mind the goats.
The goats will not mind you.

The dry riverbed runs all the way
down to Brookhollow. Home.

A drawing pinned to the wall:
a big sad fish in a violet sky.

Someone has drawn it a smile.
Then rubbed the smile out.

Violet nights for a month now.
The goats won't sleep.

Neither will I. We sit up together,
all of us, staring at the peak.

The light comes off the top of the
peak. Slow. Like a heartbeat.

Count along with it once.
You'll feel it in your teeth.

My gran said the river came out
of the mountain, singing.

Then one spring it didn't come.
Nobody up here ever said why.

I drew the thing in the sky!
It's a fish. A sad big fish.

Mum says it's only lights.
Lights don't look at you, though.

Head Office? They've never come up.
They only ever send letters.

Lovely letters. Thick paper.
I weave the envelopes into rugs.

The switchbacks start at the south
end of the village. Snow all the way.

Wrap up, {player}.
The wind up there has elbows.

Been to the Lodge yet? They sell
the Legend of Ondravel. On towels!

A kind spirit in the peak.
It's ever so cosy, the story.

Some nights the light pulses.
Some nights it just... waits.

Tonight it's waiting.
For you, maybe. Don't keep it.

Bread's fresh. The water's melted
snow. Has been for fifty years.

River water'd make a better crust.
One day. You'll see.

Welcome to the RT Heritage Lodge!
Booklets, tea towels, crystal fish.

All proceeds go to Revival Tech.
Which is lovely. For them.

THE LEGEND OF ONDRAVEL: a kind spirit
sleeps in the peak and blesses all.

"Crystal light for the valley."
You know better now.

A typed note: "This line has been
paid for. Please run it."

"Thank you so much."
No name. Of course no name.
Ride back down to Frostspire?

No letter for me. Just a note
saying the line was paid for.

Paid by who? Doesn't say. Only
says thank you. Twice, underlined.

First car up in fifty years and
I'm on it! Battle while we climb?

Look out the window. The peak
glows violet even in daylight.

A frozen waterfall. The very top
of the old river.
A cave runs in behind the ice.

RT survey crew. We all got kind
letters. "Please go and look."

I say we don't go up. Nobody's
ever that nice in a letter.

We'll argue about it later.
You go, if you're going.

Thirty winters on this pass.
This is the first violet one.

Lean into the slope, not away.
The mountain likes manners.

Rope check! Boots check!
Battle check?

My hands went numb on the last turn.
Worth it. Look at that view.

Last bend before the icefall.
You only pass if you're warm enough.

Hear it humming in the ice?
I keep thinking it's a song.

Go on up. It's waiting for you,
I think.

The signal is strongest here.
The ice hums under your hand.

In it, your team's crystals show
their own colours, not violet.

Inside a frozen waterfall! Shh.
You can hear the water, still.

It's still moving, deep in there.
Very, very slowly.

My crystals keep flickering.
Battle me before they make up minds.

Mine went blue for a second there.
Blue! Did you see?

Ice diving. Cold? Yes.
Sensible? No. Fun? Very.

There's a pool under the ice,
warm as a bath. Strange, eh?

I keep this cave. Nobody passes
who can't hold their own up there.

You'll do. Mind the spire.
It remembers things.

Teo: You found us! Snowed in.
All alive. All grumpy.

Teo: We followed the ore north.
Item one: find the source. Not done.

Marta: The bench here? A 2.
It's a log.

Marta: Go up if you must.
We'll keep the fire going.

Pell: I've drawn the spire forty
times. It looks different each time.

Pell: Today it looks tired.
Is that silly? It looks tired.

Imke hums a tune. You know it
from somewhere. A dream.

Imke: We stay here. You go.
Then come back down. Promise.

The camp fire. Warm to the bones.
Your team curls up beside it.
Your Kilu are fully healed.

A crystal door. It hums.
It isn't ready for you yet.

Find the field team first.
They're at the camp.

The door hums open for a creature
showing its own colour.

A Line 1 cot room.
Little beds, fifty years cold.

Each bed has a number.
Not one has a name.

The Test 7 room. An empty control
chair, turned to face the wall.

Violet crystal has grown over
everything here. It hums, slowly.

Facility Keeper. We only ever
got letters, too.

Kind ones. "Keep it safe."
We never asked keep what.

The stairs are sealed with crystal.
This floor's keeper holds the light.

A dome, grown solid with violet
crystal. Something huge is inside.

Its forehead crystal is cracked
and dim.

The river tune from your dream
starts to play.

{lead}'s crystal shows its own
colour. The creature watches it.

It is not ordering.
It is asking.
Put your hand on the dome?

The door reader reads your lanyard.
EMPLOYEE NOT FOUND.

...Your phone is quiet.
RITA isn't here. Not yet.

The sluice gate to the river.
The wheel is open now.

The sluice gate to the river.
Greave's staff won't let you near.

Annexe handler. Stay back!
The batch is loose!

These bands were meant to calm
them. They don't! They don't!

Who are you?
You're not on the night list!

Just get out.
Get everyone out.

Dr. Ansel Greave, Annexe Lead.
I am holding this batch.

If it goes, so do my staff's jobs.
I won't let it.

...You're right. The jobs don't
matter if the people drown.

Greave hauls the sluice wheel round.
The Line 14 batch pours out.

Into the river bend they go.
His staff run for the door.

Greave: Write it down as a field
trial. Nobody will ask.

Signal tech. Test 7 broke
something. We're trying to fix it!

Every pulse is louder.
Can you hear it? Can you?

Holt says Test 8 gets control back.
I hope she's right. I hope.
Go. Talk to Holt. Please.

A young tech by the tea trolley.
Her name tag says FINCH, C.

Coralie: You're not staff. ...Come
on. I'll open the tide door.
Coralie: What's your name?

No. Don't tell me.
I'd only have to forget it.
fin.t.coralie_name_cut.note: [SAMPLE] line kept word for word, split for length

pages:
Coralie: I made the tea.
That's all I'm meant to do tonight.

The tide door.
Coralie has left it unlocked.
The tide door is locked.

Holt: Techs only past the console.
Who let you in?

Dr. Maren Holt, Signal Lead.
Test 8 runs now.

More power, more control.
Move.

...It would have finished it.
Wouldn't it.

Holt sits down hard. She does not
reach for the console again.

Coralie pulls the Test 8 plug
herself. Her hand shakes.

She writes the last row of the run
sheet. You don't read it to her.

The Test 8 plug hangs loose.
The run sheet is full.

The Test 8 console.
Holt is standing in front of it.

Containment staff.
Nobody goes up!

Line 1 is the danger.
The Chief said so. The Chief knows.

The walls are humming.
Please. Please turn back.

The Chief holds the top landing.
You go through me first.

Go on, then. Up.
...Be gentle with it.

The Chief: Nobody reaches the
landing while my staff still stand.

The Chief: That thing is the source
of all this. It stays shut in.

It's hurting. I know.
It stays shut in.

The Chief: ...Then you go.
I won't watch.

The Chief stands aside from
the landing, eyes on the floor.

Through the window: three labs.
Their lights go out one by one.

Rain lashes the glass. Far below,
three labs blaze with light.

pages:
The dome lies open. Cold now.
Nothing inside is hurting.

OLD FORD. Flat stones to cross by,
for when the water comes back.

GOAT PEN. Please shut the gate.
The goats can open it. Just check.

RT HERITAGE LODGE & SKYLIFT
Gifts, tea, and the top lift line.

WELLSPIRE SWITCHBACKS
Cairnfold below. Icefall above.

Snow all year. Turn back if the
light in the sky starts to pulse.

A cairn of flat stones.
Each one has a name scratched in.

Climbers who made it this far.
Some are fifty years old.

A wooden post, half under water:
"RIVER BEND - NO BOATS IN FLOOD"

A depth pole. The water is past
the top mark, and still rising.

FIELD CAMP. Teo's handwriting:
"Please do not eat the map."

A log, with a note pinned to it:
"BENCH. 2/10. - M."

section2_town_npcs.name: Hester
pages:
Every hole in a net has a story.
This one's a Mirejaw. Rude fish.

Pass me that twine, {player}?
Thank you. Hands aren't what they were.
after:
Thirty years mending the same
nets. They're more knot than net now.

section2_town_npcs.name: Pip
section2_town_npcs.note: shell-collecting child on the beach corner
pages:
I've got ninety-nine shells!
One more and I'm the shell queen.

This one hums if you hold it
to your ear. It's the sea, I think.
after:
Still ninety-nine. The sea keeps
the good ones for itself.

section2_town_npcs.name: Dunmore
section2_town_npcs.note: ore trader with a full cart (ore-trade NPC)
pages:
Ore from the caldera, sold by
weight. Honest scales, mine.

Revival Tech buys all the violet
bits. Pays well. Asks nothing.
after:
Fair price is when both of us
walk off grumbling. Good day!

section2_town_npcs.name: Maud
pages:
Kilns don't sleep, so I don't.
Well. I nap. Standing up.

Pots in at dawn, out at dusk.
Crack one, and the kiln laughs.
after:
Hear the kiln ticking? It's
cooling. Best sound in town.

section2_town_npcs.name: Corrie
pages:
New stilts every spring.
The bog eats the old ones.

I drive them in, it swallows them.
We're old friends, me and the bog.
after:
Lean on a house here and it leans
back. Polite, really.

section2_town_npcs.name: Old Saul
section2_town_npcs.note: poles a flat boat between stilt houses
pages:
Need a lift across the channel?
Not today. My pole's in for repair.

Storm's coming. You can smell it.
The reeds go quiet first.
after:
Thirty years punting. Fell in
once. Don't tell the ducks.

section2_town_npcs.name: Elsie
section2_town_npcs.note: lights the boardwalk lanterns at dusk
pages:
I light the boardwalk lamps so
nobody steps off into the bog.

Those little bog lights don't
need me. They light themselves.
after:
Count the lamps on your way home.
If one's out, tell me. Please.

inspect:
HARBOUR NOTICES: "Fishing Derby,
end of the month. Bring a bucket."

"Lost: one awning. Last seen
flying past the lighthouse."

A glass case: the old keeper's log.
"Night 1. Storm. Lamp held."

"Night 2. Storm. Kettle held.
Lamp less sure."

A damp crate, lid stencilled
SIGNAL. Empty, apart from straw.

Another SIGNAL crate.
Wet tracks lead off up the quay.

Nets drying on a rack.
They smell of salt and old rope.

A bronze anvil on a plinth:
"FIRST FORGE. Lit 300 years ago."

Someone has polished the plaque.
Every single day, by the shine.

FOUNDRY ROTA: "Shift 1 - Bea.
Shift 2 - Bea. Shift 3 - Bea?"
Under it: "Bea, go home. - B.F."

An ore cart, still warm.
The rocks inside glow faintly.

Tongs, hammers, a bent file.
Each one worn to its owner's hand.

A brick kiln, ticking as it cools.
A row of pots waits inside.

TIDE BOARD, in chalk:
"High at dusk. Storm by Thursday."

Thursday is crossed out.
It says "sooner" now.

A stilt with notches cut in it.
Each one a flood, with a year.

A mossy stone frog. Someone has
put a tiny hat on it. A good hat.

Muddy boots by the door. Dozens.
The bog stays outside. Mostly.

Eel traps and reed baskets
stacked on a shelf to dry.

pages:
Each floor of the lighthouse has
its own trick. Up you go, one by one.

Here, some walls can't be seen.
Walk slow and feel for the gaps.

Up on 2F, pads come in pairs.
Step on one, pop out of its twin.

A pressure plate opens the gate to
the stairs. On 3F, too. Then the lamp.
pages_again:
2F: the plate is in the far left
room. A pad will take you there.

3F: the plate's by the stairs.
The walls make you walk round to it.

The Master waits by the lamp, on
the carpet. Say hello for me.
pages_old: The lens flashes long and short beams through four coloured panes.
Each floor has four lamps in those colours. Light them in that order.
Get it wrong and they go out. No harm done. The ghosts find it funny.

after:
Arrow boards push you the way they
point. Read the next one first.
after_2:
Past the arrows it's all walls.
A plate far left opens the gate.
after_old: The frogs croak in an order. Light the lamps the same way.

after:
Stuck going round in circles?
An arrow sent you. Try another board.
after_2:
The gate up top stays shut till
you step on the plate. West side.
after_old: Can't hear the frogs? Watch for ripples. Each one starts by a lamp.

after:
A plate opens the Master's gate.
This one's right under my feet.
after_2:
Go round below me to reach it.
I'll mind my toes.
after_old: All three crystals have to glow at once. Count before you touch.

after:
On ice you slide till something
stops you. Pick your wall first.
after_2:
This maze has a plate in its
middle. It opens the gate up north.
after_old:
Stand where the gusts cross
and you'll go nowhere fast.

after:
Through the gate? Good. Ice again.
Slide to a wall, then turn.
after_2:
Up the left side, then along the
top. The Master's waiting.
after_old:
The Master reads the wind first,
the challenger second.

pages:
Arrow boards push you the way they
point. Look before you step.

Past them, a maze. A plate in it
opens the gate to Wenna.
pages_old: It's dark on the water. Light a reed lamp and you'll see the planks near it.
The frogs croak in an order. Light the lamps in that same order.
Can't hear them? Watch the water. Every croak leaves a ripple by its lamp.
